speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: asked the Minister for Education (a) whether the Ministry will provide an update on the Strategic Partnership Co-Curricular Activity (SP-CCA) programme; (b) whether this programme will be extended to more sports and arts activities; (c) whether the programme will be extended to primary schools; and (d) whether the Ministry will work together with National Sports Associations to deliver sports through the SP-CCA programme.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Education)
text: The programme had to be redesigned into a hybrid format during the COVID-19 pandemic to minimise inter-school interactions for safety of our students.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Education)
text: SP-CCA has been offered to Secondary school students who are older and who can make their way to practice venues outside their schools.

speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Education)
text: The SP-CCA athletics and water polo programmes leverage the expertise provided by SportSG.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
text: I think it is a very useful tool, especially, with some of the schools not having the resources as well as the number of athletes or participants to form a full team or the CCAs.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
text: First, what are the considerations for sports uniform group or visual and performing arts programmes to be included as an SP-CCA programme?

speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
text: Would the consideration for strategic national representation or high performance be made a consideration, including such sports or programmes?

speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
text: I think this comes from like team sports, for example, where you cannot really form a team; or take, for example, diving or gymnastics, where we have athletes going to the Olympic games, and not all schools provide these CCAs.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
text: I think the number of schools are reducing.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
text: The second supplementary question is on the current SP-CCA programme.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
text: How is MOE engaging SportSG to ensure the delivery of these programmes are aligned to the curriculum prescribed by MOE, as these are co-curricular activities?

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: At the end of the day, we want to allow our students with different talent to be able to flourish and develop their talent.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: We also note that the students themselves need to indicate their preferences, need to be able to travel outside of their schools.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: We know that for some of our students, they want to do CCAs within their own schools so that they can be with their friends, so that they can play sports and do activities with people whom they know.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: We cannot force the students to go for sports and arts, just because we think it is strategic and it is something that we want them to be good at.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: At the end of the day, we have to respect the students' choices.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: I did not quite get the Member's second question.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: Can you repeat that please, Mr Mark Chay?

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: On the first supplementary question, it is more like, giving them an option.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: National Sports Associations (NSAs) can play a part in delivering these co-curricular activities through SP-CCA programmes.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: We are not forcing any students to choose.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: If they so choose to, then it is great.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: It will be good to have the opportunity to have these programmes at the Primary school level as well as the Secondary school level.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: The second question is, these are co-curricular activities.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: Presumably, there is a curriculum for CCAs to be delivered; there are some things or outcomes that will be delivered through the CCAs.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: How are these delivered through these SP-CCA programmes and how are these communicated to SportSG so that these outcomes are delivered through CCAs?
